lessons.title: э (e) — the e that opens этот
lessons.gloss: e — the e that opens этот

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on, your eyes, for letter shapes on the page and your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Warm-up, Script you'll notice: э and Guided Practice.

segments.text: Before the new one: write я and ё once each, and name them.
Now say этот (étot), "this". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.

It opens этот (étot), "this", and эта. It looks like a с turned to face the other way, with a short bar across the middle. It is the plain e sound, with no y in front of it, which is why it is mostly found at the start of a word.
Follow the numbered strip: start where movement 1 begins, and let each panel show you the next movement before your pen makes it. Then write э yourself — slowly, and larger than it is printed.
The strip shows where to start this letter and which way to travel, in one attested order, and names its source beneath it. Teachers vary, so treat it as a sound way in, not the only one.

segments.instruction: at этот and point at э inside it
segments.source: [YOU LOOK: at **этот** and point at э inside it]

segments.instruction: э three times, saying e as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: э three times, saying *e* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: ё, then э, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — э? (e, e.) Which word did it come from? (этот, étot, "this".)

segments.text: Before the new one: write ё and э once each, and name them.
Now say площадь (plóshchad), "a square". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
It is inside площадь (plóshchad), "a square". It is ш with a small tail at the bottom right, and it sounds like a long, soft sh.

Follow the numbered strip: start where movement 1 begins, and let each panel show you the next movement before your pen makes it. Then write щ (shcha) yourself — slowly, and larger than it is printed.
The strip shows where to start this letter and which way to travel, in one attested order, and names its source beneath it. Teachers vary, so treat it as a sound way in, not the only one.

segments.instruction: at площадь and point at щ (shcha) inside it

segments.instruction: щ (shcha) three times, saying shch as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: щ three times, saying *shch* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: э, then щ, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — щ? (shcha, shch.) Which word did it come from? (площадь, plóshchad, "a square".)
